[[Rockville, Maryland]], U.S. |college= [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|University of Maryland]] (2006–2010) }} '''Greivis Vasquez''' ({{Birth date|mf=yes|1987|1|16}}) is a [[Venezuela]]n [[basketball]] player who ended his [[College basketball|U.S. college]] career with the [[University of Maryland, College Park|University of Maryland]] [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|men's basketball team]] in 2010. Vasquez finished second on the Terrapins' all-time scoring list, with 2,171 career points.[http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/player/profile?playerId=32018 Greivis Vasquez stats] He was born in [[Caracas]] and moved to the United States to attend high school at [[Montrose Christian School]] in [[Rockville, Maryland]] in 2004.Tysiac, Ken. [http://www.sportingnews.com/yourturn/viewtopic.php?t=311763 "Q&A with Maryland guard Greivis Vasquez"], ''[[Sporting News]]'', November 29, 2007. Accessed December 1, 2007. "Q: What was Kevin Durant like when you played with him at Montrose Christian?" During his senior year at Montrose, he committed to The University of Maryland to play under head coach [[Gary Williams]]. In 2007, Vasquez played on the [[Venezuela national basketball team|Venezuelan national basketball team]] in the FIBA America Championships. In his final college season of [[2009–10 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2009–10]], he was one of three Venezuelans playing in [[Division I (NCAA)|NCAA Division I]] men's basketball, with the others being [[David Cubillan]] of the [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette Golden Eagles]] and Gregory Echenique of the [[Creighton Bluejays men's basketball|Creighton Bluejays]]. ==Childhood and Schooling== Vasquez grew up in Caracas, Venezuela, where he lived with his parents, Ivis Rodriguez and Gregorio Vasquez, and brother, Ingerman Sanoya. At Montrose Christian, Vasquez played under head coach Stu Vetter, and helped the Mustangs post a 43–5 record over his junior and senior seasons. While at Montrose Christian he played with future college and NBA star [[Kevin Durant]]. ==College Career== ===Freshman Year (2006–07)=== In the beginning of his freshman year (2006–07), Vasquez did not start for the Terps, but still played solid minutes. Midway through the season, he began starting at the [[2 guard]] position, alongside fellow freshman Eric Hayes at the starting [[point guard]] position. He remained a starter for the rest of the season. He heavily contributed to the Terrapins' six-game winning streak at the end of the season, giving Maryland a #4 seed in the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|NCAA Tournament]]. Vasquez averaged 9.8 points, 4.7 assists, and 3.3 rebounds per game during his freshman season, and shooting percentages of 44.4 for field goals, 31.6 for three-pointers, and 79.8 for free throws. ===Sophomore Year (2007–08)=== Vasquez had per-game averages of 17 points, 6.8 assists, and 5.7 rebounds, and shooting percentages of 43.2 for field goals, 30.9 for three-pointers, and 78.2 for free throws.[http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/player/profile?playerId=32018 Greivis Vasquez stats] ===Junior Year (2008–09)=== As a junior, Vasquez led the Terrapins in scoring (17.5), rebounds (5.4), assists (5.0), steals (1.40), and minutes (34.6 per game). He became the first Terrapin basketball player to ever lead the team in points, rebounds and assists in a single season, and only the 6th player to ever accomplish that task in the ACC. On February 21, 2009, Vasquez registered a then career-high 35 points, to go along with 11 rebounds and 10 assists—Maryland's third [[triple-double]] in history and the first since 1987—in a come-from-behind 88–85 overtime win over [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|UNC]].[http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=290520120 Vasquez records triple-double to lead Maryland's rally past No. 3 UNC] {{cite news|url=http://www.interbasket.net/news/1072/2009/02/21/greivis-vasquez-maryland-shocks-3-north-carolina|title=Greivis Vasquez, Maryland upsets North Carolina|publisher=Interbasket.net|date=February 21, 2009}} At the end of his junior year, Vasquez ranked 7th in scoring, 3rd in FT percentage (.867), 3rd in assists per game, 3rd in assist/turnover ratio (1.80), and 5th in minutes per game in the ACC. He reached double-figures in scoring in 57 of his last 61 games, including his last 17. In Maryland's final 10 games, he had five 20-point games as well.{{cite news|url=http://www.umterps.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/vasquez_greivis00.html|title=Greivis Vasquez Basketball Profile|publisher=UMTerps.com}} He was named Second-Team All-ACC at the close of the regular season.{{cite news|url=http://weblogs.baltimoresun.com/sports/college/maryland_terps/blog/2009/03/greivis_named_secondteam_allacc.html|title=Greivis Vasquez named second-team All-ACC|publisher=baltimoresun.com}} ===Senior Year (2009–10)=== As a senior, Vasquez averaged 19.6 points, 6.3 assists, 4.6 rebounds, and 1.7 steals per game over 33 games. Vasquez is the only player in the country to average more than 18 points and 6 assists per game. His honors included the 2010 [[Bob Cousy Award]] given by the [[Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame]] to the nation's best collegiate point guard, for which he edged out [[Sherron Collins]] (Kansas), [[Scottie Reynolds]] (Villanova), [[Jon Scheyer]] (Duke), [[Evan Turner]] (Ohio State), and [[John Wall (basketball)|John Wall]] (Kentucky).{{cite news| url=http://voices.washingtonpost.com/terrapins-insider/2010/03/vasquez_named_one_of_six_cousy.html | work=The Washington Post | title=Vasquez named one of six Cousy Award finalists | accessdate=May 4, 2010}} Against [[2009–10 Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball team|Georgia Tech]] on February 20, 2010, Vasquez scored the 2,000th point of his collegiate career, making him the only player in ACC history to compile at least 2,000 points, 700 assists, and 600 rebounds.{{cite news|url=http://www.wtop.com/?nid=177&sid=1893484|title=Maryland squeezes past Georgia Tech 76–74 |last=Ginsburg|first=David|date=February 20, 2010|work=Associated Press|publisher= |accessdate=February 21, 2010}} The following week, Vasquez set a new career scoring high with 41 points in the Terrapins' double-overtime victory at [[2009–10 Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball team|Virginia Tech]].{{cite news|url=http://www.baltimoresun.com/sports/terps/bal-marylandhoops0227,0,301470.story|title=Terps outlast Va. Tech in double overtime|publisher=Baltimore Sun|date=February 27, 2010}} Vasquez also scored 20 points in Maryland's home win over [[2009–10 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]] on Senior Night, and made several critical baskets and assists in the final minutes to secure a victory. Vazquez helped lead Maryland to a 13–3 conference record to tie Duke for the regular season ACC championship. He was named a unanimous first-team All-ACC selection on March 8, 2010, and the [[Atlantic Coast Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|ACC Player of the Year]] on March 9, 2010, beating out Duke's [[Jon Scheyer]] and Virginia Tech's [[Malcolm Delaney]]. {{cite news|url=http://www.theacc.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030810aac.html|title=ACC Announces 2009–10 All-ACC Teams}}{{cite news|url=http://www.theacc.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030910aaa.html|title=Terrapins' Vasquez Named ACC Player of the Year|date=March 9, 2010|work=TheACC.com|accessdate=March 9, 2010}} Vasquez also won three ACC Player of the Week honors in his final season, which brought his career total to seven. {{cite news|url=http://www.theacc.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/022210aaa.html|title=Maryland's Greivis Vasquez and Georgia Tech's Derrick Favors earn ACC Basketball Honors|date=February 22, 2010|work=TheACC.com|accessdate=April 5, 2010}} ==See also== * [[2010 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans]] ==References== {{Reflist|2}} {{Bob Cousy Award}} {{2010 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans}} {{ACC Men's Basketball POY}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Vasquez, Greivis}} [[Category:1987 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Venezuelan basketball players]] [[Category:Venezuelan expatriate basketball people in the United States]] [[Category:Maryland Terrapins men's basketball players]] [[Category:People from Caracas]] [[Category:Point guards]] [[es:Greivis Vásquez]] [[ja:グレイビス・バスケス]]
